questions_and_answers.question: What type of stem is 'meist-' in German?
What does 'die meiste Zeit' mean in the sentence 'Die meiste Zeit arbeitet er überhaupt nicht'?
Which sentence uses 'meisten' correctly as an attributive adjective?

answers.answer: Meistens essen wir um ein Uhr.

questions_and_answers.question: In 'Herr Köhler raucht am meisten', what does 'am meisten' express?
How does the adverb 'meistens' differ from 'meisten'?

answers.answer: 'meistens' is an adverb and never part of a phrase, whereas 'meisten' occurs in phrases with specifiers

questions_and_answers.question: Which translation best matches 'Von allen Verwandten besucht uns meine Tante am meisten'?

answers.answer: From all relatives my aunt visits us the most
Among all relatives my aunt is the last to visit us
My aunt visits us rarely among all relatives
My relatives visit my aunt the most

questions_and_answers.question: In the sentences 'Die meisten sagen nichts' and 'Meistens sagen sie nichts', what is the difference between 'die meisten' and 'meistens'?

answers.answer: 'die meisten' is an adverb and 'meistens' is an adjective
'die meisten' is singular and 'meistens' is plural

questions_and_answers.question: Which sentence uses 'meistens' correctly to mean 'usually'?

answers.answer: Er hat meistens Geld von uns allen.

questions_and_answers.question: What is emphasised about 'meisten' and 'meistens' in the notes?

answers.answer: 'Meisten' always occurs in a phrase and 'meistens' never is part of a phrase
'Meistens' is used before nouns and 'meisten' after verbs

questions_and_answers.question: Which of the following sentences uses 'am meisten' to express a superlative?

answers.answer: Wir essen meistens um ein Uhr.

articles.text:
E. THE SUPERLATIVE STEM MEIST-
Meist- was noted as an irregular superlative stem in Unit 9. We have encountered some of the forms in which it occurs and will now add a few more examples in order to present a summary of its forms and their uses.
1. As attributive adjectives, forms of the stem *meist-* occur in the specifier‑adjective‑noun sequence:
Essen nicht die meisten Leute mittags ihre Hauptmahlzeit? – Don’t most people eat their main meal at noon?
Die meiste Zeit arbeitet er überhaupt nicht. – Most of the time he doesn’t work at all.
Das meiste Geschirr will ich in Deutschland kaufen. – Most of the china I intend to buy in Germany.
Von uns allen hat er das meiste Geld. – Of all of us he has the most money.
Die meisten sagen gar nichts. – Most people don’t say anything at all.
Notice that in English we say “most,” “the most,” or “most of the…”. The forms of *meist-* in an attributive phrase in German are always preceded by a specifier. The noun can be omitted, however.
2. The special predicate phrase *am meisten*:
Herr Köhler raucht am meisten.
Abends lese ich am meisten.
Von allen Verwandten besucht uns meine Tante am meisten.
3. The adverb *meistens*:
Wir essen meistens um ein Uhr.
Er schreibt meistens Romane.
Im Sommer fahren wir meistens ins Gebirge.
Mr. Köhler smokes the most.
I read most in the evenings.
Of all our relatives my aunt visits us the most.
We usually eat at one o’clock.
He writes mostly novels.
In the summer we usually go to the mountains.
Compare the sentences above and note the different meanings given by the forms of *meist-*. Note especially the difference in the way the two forms *meisten* and *meistens* are used: *Meisten* ALWAYS occurs in a phrase. *Meistens* NEVER is part of a phrase.
Die meisten sagen nichts. / Meistens sagen sie nichts. / Am meisten lese ich abends. / Meistens lese ich abends.
Most say nothing. / Mostly they say nothing. / I read most in the evenings. / Usually I read in the evenings.
